subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Roughly which years span the Baroque period in Western music?
questions.explain: The Baroque period is conventionally dated from around 1600 to the death of J.S. Bach in 1750.

questions.q: What are the dates of Johann Sebastian Bach?
questions.explain: Bach, a leading Baroque composer, lived from 1685 to 1750.

questions.q: What are the dates of Ludwig van Beethoven?
questions.explain: Beethoven lived from 1770 to 1827, bridging the Classical and Romantic eras.

questions.q: Which work by Bach is the set work for Instrumental Music 1700-1820?
options: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
questions.explain: The Edexcel Bach set work is the third movement of the Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 in D major.

questions.q: In which key is the third movement of Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5?
questions.explain: The whole concerto, including its third movement, is in the tonic key of D major.

questions.q: The Beethoven set work is the first movement of which piece?
questions.explain: The set work is the first movement of Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8 in C minor 'Pathétique', Op. 13.

questions.q: In which key is Beethoven's 'Pathétique' Sonata?
questions.explain: The 'Pathétique' Sonata is in the dramatic key of C minor.

questions.q: Which keyboard instrument typically realises the basso continuo in Baroque music?
questions.explain: The harpsichord, often with a bass instrument, commonly plays the continuo in Baroque ensembles.

questions.q: In a concerto grosso, what is the 'concertino'?
questions.explain: The concertino is the small solo group, contrasted with the ripieno (full ensemble or tutti).

questions.q: What are 'terraced dynamics', a feature of Baroque style?
options: Sudden shifts between loud and soft levels
Dynamics marked only for the soloist
questions.explain: Terraced dynamics move abruptly between distinct levels rather than gradually swelling or fading.

questions.q: What is the function of the basso continuo in Baroque music?
options: To provide a continuous bass line and harmonic support
To play the main melody throughout
To double the soloist an octave higher
questions.explain: The continuo supplies an ongoing bass line and filled-in chords underpinning the harmony.

questions.q: Which three instruments make up the concertino in Brandenburg Concerto No. 5?
questions.explain: The soloists are the transverse flute, violin and a strikingly prominent harpsichord.

questions.q: What best describes 'ritornello' form?
options: A recurring main theme alternates with contrasting episodes
A theme is stated once and never returns
Two subjects are developed then recapitulated
A single melody is varied continuously
questions.explain: In ritornello form a returning tutti theme frames contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: What are the three main sections of sonata form?
questions.explain: Sonata form presents themes in the exposition, transforms them in the development, then restates them in the recapitulation.

questions.q: Compared with the Baroque harpsichord, why did the Classical fortepiano suit Beethoven's style?
options: It could play gradual crescendos and a wide dynamic range
It could only play at one fixed volume
It could not sustain notes at all
questions.explain: The fortepiano allowed graded dynamics and expressive contrasts the harpsichord could not produce.

questions.q: What is an 'Alberti bass', a common Classical accompaniment device?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand
A sustained drone in the bass
A walking bass line moving in crotchets
questions.explain: An Alberti bass breaks a chord into a repeating low-high-middle-high pattern to accompany a melody.

questions.q: You hear a flute, violin and harpsichord playing as soloists against a full string ensemble. Which set work is this most likely to be?
questions.explain: That concertino of flute, violin and harpsichord against ripieno strings is the hallmark of Brandenburg 5.

questions.q: A performer sees the marking 'Allegro di molto e con brio'. How should they play?
questions.explain: 'Allegro di molto e con brio' directs a very quick, spirited performance.

questions.q: A solo piano movement opens with a slow, dramatic C minor introduction marked 'Grave' that later returns. Which set work is this?
questions.explain: The 'Pathétique' first movement opens with a Grave introduction in C minor that recurs within the movement.

questions.q: A harpsichordist is given only a bass line with figures beneath it and improvises the chords above. What are they doing?
questions.explain: Reading a figured bass and improvising the harmonies above it is called realising the continuo.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Music (1MU0) specification; Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music 1700-1820
